oauth.alternatives: For your own workspace only, you can install the app and use the bot token it gives you. That does not work for other workspaces: each one needs its own OAuth install.

appTypes.name: Internal app (installed only in your own workspace)
appTypes.whenToUse: Prototyping, or a customer who builds the app inside their own workspace. Keeps the normal conversations.history limits (50+ requests a minute, up to 1,000 messages per call).

appTypes.name: Unlisted distributed app (public distribution on, not in the Marketplace)
appTypes.whenToUse: Pilots and early customers. Any workspace can install it with no review, but new installs can call conversations.history and conversations.replies only once a minute for 15 messages.

appTypes.name: Slack Marketplace app
appTypes.whenToUse: Commercial distribution at scale. Needs 10 active workspaces before you can submit, then a review that Slack says can take about 12 weeks. Restores normal history limits.

appTypes.name: Org-ready app (Enterprise orgs)
appTypes.whenToUse: Customers on Enterprise Grid who want one install across many workspaces. You opt in to org-level apps and an Org Admin approves the install.

verdict.label: Self-serve, optional review
verdict.summary: Any workspace can install your app without review once you turn on public distribution, but the deciding factor is the read limit: until Slack lists you in the Marketplace, new installs can read history only once a minute, 15 messages at a time. An agent that summarizes threads works for a pilot, and in practice needs a Marketplace listing for production.
verdict.nextStep: Create an app at api.slack.com/apps, install it to your own workspace, and design your reads around message events so the history limit does not stall your pilot.
verdict.customerSideGateNote: Workspace owners can require approval for every app, so members can only request your app until an admin approves it. On Enterprise Grid, an org app management policy turns on approval for each workspace, and org-wide installs need an Org Admin.

composio.note: Composio lists Slack (and a separate Slackbot toolkit) with managed OAuth, so you can start without your own Slack app. Users then see Composio on the install screen and you share its quota. Bring your own app when you need your name on the install screen, custom scopes, or your own rate limits. When you switch, only new connections use your app; existing users stay on the old one until they reconnect. Check with Composio whether its Slack app is Marketplace-listed, since that decides which history limit you get.

stages.name: Prototype
stages.whoCanConnect: Your own workspace only. The app is not distributed yet.
stages.notes: Internal apps keep the normal history limits, so this is the place to test summarization quality. Use a free developer sandbox if you need paid-plan features like the agent container.

stages.name: Limited beta
stages.whoCanConnect: Any workspace, through your Add to Slack button or install link, unless its admins require approval.
stages.notes: No Slack review. You wait only on customer admins who require app approval, and that wait is outside your control. New installs get 1 request a minute and 15 messages per call on conversations.history and conversations.replies. Slack says unlisted distribution is meant for pilots and early customers.

stages.name: Production
stages.whoCanConnect: Any workspace, from the Slack Marketplace, with normal history limits.
stages.notes: Before you can submit, the app must be installed on 10 active workspaces and stay there for the whole review. Slack says preliminary feedback takes up to 10 business days and functional review up to 10 weeks for a new app. Resubmitting during the preliminary stage resets your place in the queue. We found no developer reports we could verify, so the realistic wait has no upper bound here.

scopeTiers.name: Reply and post as a bot
scopeTiers.effect: Works in any workspace with no review. Your agent reacts to mentions and direct messages through events and posts replies. Tokens do not expire unless you turn on rotation.

scopeTiers.name: Read channels in real time (events)
scopeTiers.effect: No review while unlisted. Message events arrive as they happen in channels your bot was added to, so a pilot can read new messages without calling conversations.history. Fetching an older thread on demand still hits the 1 per minute limit.

scopeTiers.name: Read history and threads on demand at full speed
scopeTiers.effect: conversations.history and conversations.replies run at normal limits only for internal apps and Marketplace apps. For any other workspace you need a Marketplace listing, which puts *:history scopes under enhanced review.

scopeTiers.name: Search and admin
scopeTiers.effect: Slack calls these restricted scopes. Marketplace apps that use them are generally rejected, and admin.* is unlikely to pass unless you are in Slack's partner program. Use the Real-time Search API path instead if you need search.

requirements.item: A Slack account and a workspace where you can install apps
requirements.detail: The developer portal needs you to sign in. A free developer sandbox works if your own workspace limits app installs.
The redirect_uri must use HTTPS, match or sit under a configured Redirect URL, and contain no #. Send the same value in the authorize and token steps.

requirements.item: A real OAuth install flow, not a hard-coded token
requirements.detail: Each workspace gets its own token from oauth.v2.access. Store tokens per workspace and per user.
Events API, interactivity, slash commands, and options load URLs all need SSL before you can distribute.

requirements.item: Reads that survive 1 request a minute
requirements.detail: Unlisted installs get 15 messages per call to conversations.history and conversations.replies. Read new messages from events, and queue history fetches.

requirements.item: 10 active workspaces with your app installed
requirements.detail: Active means used in the last 28 days and not a sandbox. You must stay at 10 or more for the whole review.

requirements.item: Public landing page, privacy policy, and support page
requirements.detail: The privacy policy must say what you collect, how you use it, how long you keep it, and how users ask for deletion, with an email or form. Support must answer within 2 business days.
Only scopes for features that exist today. *:history scopes get enhanced review.

requirements.item: AI disclosures and no model training on Slack data
requirements.detail: Disclose the model, retention, and data residency in your listing, warn that output can be wrong, and never train a model on Slack data. Apps using the agent container should not store Slack data.
Name, short description of 10 words or fewer, long description, icon, screenshots at 1600x1000 under 2MB, and a recommended 30 to 90 second video.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Sign in at api.slack.com/apps and click Create New App. Pick From scratch or From a manifest, name it, and choose your development workspace. You land on the app's Basic Information page with a client ID and secret.

steps.title: Add scopes and the redirect URL
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions, add bot scopes such as chat:write, app_mentions:read, and channels:history, and add your HTTPS redirect URL (for example your Composio callback). Mark scopes that are nice to have as optional so users can decline them.

steps.title: Turn on the agent features you need
steps.detail: If you want the split-view agent container, turn on the Agents & AI Apps feature in app settings. This adds assistant:write. The container needs a paid plan, so test in a sandbox and make sure the app still works on free plans.

steps.title: Subscribe to message events
steps.detail: Under Event Subscriptions, set an HTTPS request URL and subscribe to app_mention, message.im, and message.channels. Your agent can then read new messages as they arrive instead of polling history.

steps.title: Install to your workspace and test
steps.detail: Install from the app settings, invite the bot to a test channel, and check that you can summarize a thread and post a reply. Internal installs have normal history limits.

steps.title: Build the OAuth install flow
steps.detail: Send users to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with your client ID, scopes, state, and redirect_uri. Check state on return, exchange the code with oauth.v2.access within 10 minutes, and store the token by team or enterprise ID.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation now
steps.detail: Rotation gives 12-hour access tokens and single-use refresh tokens. It cannot be turned off once on. Without it, tokens do not expire. If you use Composio or another broker, confirm it handles rotated Slack tokens before you switch it on.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Open Manage Distribution, complete the checklist (OAuth flow, HTTPS URLs, no hard-coded tokens), and click Activate Public Distribution. You get an Add to Slack button and a shareable install link.

steps.title: Opt in to org-level installs if you sell to Enterprise Grid
steps.detail: Add a bot scope like team:read, select Opt-In under Org Level Apps, and handle is_enterprise_install in the token response. An Org Admin then installs the app and picks workspaces.

steps.title: Send pilots the admin approval note
steps.detail: Many workspaces require app approval. Give each pilot customer the admin note draft so their workspace owner approves the app instead of ignoring the request.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Keep at least 10 workspaces using the app in the last 28 days. Sandboxes do not count. You need to stay at 10 through the whole review.

steps.title: Prepare the listing and submit
steps.detail: Publish the landing, privacy, and support pages. In Submit to the Slack Marketplace, pass the automated checks, add the listing, scope reasons, test account details, and a demo video of install, use, and uninstall.

steps.title: Wait for preliminary and functional review
steps.detail: Slack checks your listing first, then a reviewer installs the app in their own workspace and tests it. Answer all feedback. Slack will not speed up review for a launch date.

blockers.symptom: conversations.history returns only 15 messages and you get ratelimited errors after one call a minute.
blockers.cause: Your app is distributed but not in the Marketplace, so new installs have the reduced limit.
blockers.fix: Read new messages from events, cache only thread IDs and cursors, and queue history fetches. For full speed, get Marketplace approval. Internal installs keep normal limits.
blockers.escalation: Ask Slack developer support whether your app counts as commercially distributed.

blockers.symptom: Members click Add to Slack and can only send a request.
blockers.fix: Ask the customer's workspace owner or app manager to approve the app. Send them the admin note draft with your scope list.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri differs between the authorize and oauth.v2.access calls, or is not under a configured Redirect URL.
blockers.fix: Send the exact same HTTPS redirect_uri in both steps and add it under OAuth & Permissions.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace submission is blocked or returned before review starts.
blockers.cause: Fewer than 10 active workspaces, or you dropped below 10 during review.
blockers.fix: Grow pilot installs first. Count only workspaces used in the last 28 days that are not sandboxes.

blockers.cause: History scopes get enhanced review, and broad access without a clear use case is unlikely to pass.
blockers.fix: Request history only for channels the bot is added to, explain the exact feature in the scope reason, and show it in the demo video.

blockers.symptom: Your app stops working in a workspace after a person leaves.
blockers.cause: Apps with scopes beyond bot, commands, webhooks, or identify are uninstalled when the installing user leaves or becomes a guest.
blockers.fix: Listen for app_uninstalled and prompt the workspace to reinstall. Prefer bot scopes so installs do not depend on one person.

blockers.symptom: invalid_refresh_token or tokens stop working after 12 hours.
blockers.cause: Token rotation is on and you reused an old refresh token. Each one works only once.
blockers.fix: Always store the newest refresh token from each refresh. Rotation cannot be turned off.

blockers.cause: Some scopes cannot be used for org-level installs.
blockers.fix: Remove the scope or use a workspace-level install for that customer.

didForYou: Read about 21 official Slack and Composio pages and the Slack changelog, and tied each claim to its source.
Probed slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with an invalid client ID: it answers 200 with a page that redirects through a script.
Checked api.slack.com/apps: it loads and asks you to sign in before you can create an app.
Drafted a channels:history scope reason, an admin approval note, an app description, and a privacy checklist.
canDoForYou: Write an app manifest with your scopes, events, redirect URL, and agent settings.
Write the OAuth flow, state check, token storage, and rotation handling.
Build an events-first reader and a rate-limited queue for history calls.
Draft listing copy, scope reasons, AI disclosures, and a demo video script.
Fill app settings in a browser while you watch, after you sign in.
youMustDo: Sign in to Slack and create the app.
Decide whether to turn on token rotation, since it is permanent.
Get pilot customers and their admins to install and approve the app.
Publish a privacy policy and support page you stand behind.
Record the demo video and submit to the Marketplace.
Accept Slack's API terms, including the ban on training models with Slack data.

drafts.title: channels:history scope reason (Marketplace)
drafts.body:
DRAFT, edit before use.

Scope: channels:history (bot token)

[App name] is an AI assistant that summarizes threads and drafts replies in Slack. When a user mentions @[App name] in a thread, or clicks Summarize thread in the message menu, we call conversations.replies for that one thread and show a summary in the thread.

We only read public channels the bot has been added to. We do not read channels the bot is not in, and we do not bulk read or export history.

We do not store message text. We keep only channel and thread IDs so we can link back to the thread. Message text is sent to [model provider] only to produce the summary, and it is not used to train any model.

Without this scope, the core feature (thread summaries) does not work.

To test: install the app, invite @[App name] to a channel, start a thread with a few replies, then mention @[App name] summarize in the thread.

drafts.title: Note to a workspace admin asking for approval
drafts.body:
DRAFT, edit before use.

Hi [admin name],

I requested approval for [App name] in our Slack workspace. It is an AI assistant that summarizes threads and drafts replies when someone mentions it.

What it can access:
- Messages in public channels only after someone adds the bot to that channel (channels:history)
- Mentions of the app and direct messages to it (app_mentions:read, im:history)
- Posting replies as the bot (chat:write)

What it does not do: it does not read channels it was not added to, it does not export messages, and the vendor states it does not train AI models on our data. Their privacy policy is at [URL] and security details are at [URL].

You can approve it under Admin, Apps and workflows, App management settings. We can remove it at any time from the same place.

Thanks,
[Your name]

drafts.title: Marketplace short and long description
drafts.body:
DRAFT, edit before use.

Short (10 words or fewer): Summarize Slack threads and draft replies with AI.

Long: [App name] helps your team catch up fast. Mention @[App name] in any thread to get a short summary of decisions and open questions, or ask it to draft a reply you can edit before posting.

How it works in Slack: add the bot to the channels you want. It reads only those channels, and only when someone asks.

AI notice: summaries are generated by [model] and can be wrong. Check important details in the thread. Slack data is not stored after the summary is made and is never used to train models.

drafts.title: Privacy policy and listing checklist for Slack
drafts.body:
DRAFT, edit before use.

- What Slack data you collect (message text, user IDs, channel IDs).
- How you use it, in plain words.
- How long you keep it. If you keep nothing after a reply, say so.
- Data you receive but never use, stated as such.
- How a user or admin asks for access, transfer, or deletion.
- A contact email or web form, not only a postal address.
- The AI model you use, where it runs, and whether the provider keeps the data.
- A clear statement that Slack data is not used to train models.
- Support page that is public and needs no extra account, with a reply within 2 business days.

uncertainties.question: Do the reduced history limits now apply to installs made before May 29, 2025?
uncertainties.why: Slack's changelog says existing installs are not affected. A community article says the grace period ended on March 3, 2026, but it cites no Slack source and we found none.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Slack developer support, or check the rate limit headers on an old install of an unlisted app.

uncertainties.question: Does the 1 per minute limit apply to user tokens as well as bot tokens?
uncertainties.why: The changelog describes the limit per app and does not mention token type.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Slack developer support, or test both token types on an unlisted install.

uncertainties.question: How long does Marketplace review take in practice?
uncertainties.why: Slack states up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks. We could not open any developer report to confirm it, and the submission page shows its own estimate after sign-in.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Read the estimate on your app's submission page, or ask other Slack partners.

uncertainties.question: Is Composio's managed Slack app listed in the Marketplace?
uncertainties.why: If it is not, managed connections get the reduced history limits. Composio's docs do not say.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Composio support, or check the Slack Marketplace for Composio's app.

uncertainties.question: Does a free pilot count as commercial distribution?
uncertainties.why: Slack's terms name the Marketplace as the only proper channel for commercial distribution, and the rate limit targets commercially distributed apps. The line for free or trial use is not defined on the pages we read.
uncertainties.howToResolve: Ask Slack developer support before a large unlisted rollout.

evidence.claim: Slack uses OAuth v2 at slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize. The redirect_uri must be HTTPS, match or sit under a configured Redirect URL, and match between steps or you get bad_redirect_uri. Codes expire after 10 minutes. Tokens do not expire unless rotation is on. Some scopes fail org installs with scope_not_allowed_on_enterprise.

After you activate public distribution, any workspace can install the app unless it limits installs to admins, to Marketplace apps, or requires admin approval. Redirect, events, and interactivity URLs need SSL. Unlisted distribution is meant for pilots and early customers.
Apps with scopes other than bot, incoming-webhook, commands, or identify are uninstalled when the installing user leaves the workspace or becomes a guest.

From May 29, 2025, new unlisted apps and new installs of existing unlisted apps can call conversations.history and conversations.replies 1 time a minute with a limit of 15 objects. Marketplace apps are not affected. Internal customer-built apps keep 50+ a minute and 1,000 objects.
evidence.sourceTitle: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps

evidence.claim: Slack's changelog says the new limits are not applied to existing installations of unlisted apps.
evidence.sourceTitle: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps

evidence.claim: The updated API terms name the Slack Marketplace as the only appropriate channel for commercially distributing apps, including unlisted ones. Slack says the history limit is meant to stop bulk data exfiltration by unvetted apps.
evidence.sourceTitle: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps (FAQ)

evidence.claim: Marketplace apps with fewer than 10 active workspaces and fewer than 10 weekly active users are unsuitable. *:history, files:read, search:read.* and admin.* scopes get enhanced review. Restricted scopes such as search:read and admin.* are generally rejected.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack Marketplace app guidelines and requirements

evidence.claim: Marketplace AI apps must not train models on Slack data, must disclose the model and data retention, must warn about inaccurate output, and apps using the agent container must disclose the paid plan need and should not store Slack data.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack Marketplace app guidelines and requirements

evidence.claim: Listings need a short description of 10 words or fewer, 1600x1000 images under 2MB, a public landing page, a privacy policy covering collection, use, retention, and deletion, and support that answers within 2 business days.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack Marketplace app guidelines and requirements

evidence.claim: Preliminary review feedback takes up to 10 business days and functional review up to 10 weeks for new apps (6 weeks for updates). Resubmitting in the preliminary stage resets your queue place. Slack does not expedite for launch dates.
Reviewers install the app in their own workspace, test install, OAuth, use, and uninstall, and check a reason for each scope. A demo video is recommended.
As of July 2026, Marketplace submissions need at least 10 installs on active workspaces, up from a temporary lower threshold, and must stay at 10 or more for the whole review.
evidence.sourceTitle: Updated installation requirement for Slack Marketplace apps

evidence.claim: Slack's API terms (effective 10 October 2025) bar using API data to train a large language model and bar bulk export without a separate agreement.
evidence.note: The terms also bar persistent copies and indexes of other organizations' data for the Data Access and Real-time Search APIs.

evidence.claim: With token rotation, access tokens last 12 hours and each refresh token works once. Rotation cannot be turned off once on. Without rotation, access tokens never expire.
PKCE became generally available on March 30, 2026. Enabling it marks the app as a public client and cannot be undone without support. Refresh tokens for PKCE apps expire after 30 days.

Workspace owners can require approved apps under App management settings. Members then request apps and owners or app managers approve them. On Enterprise Grid, an org app management policy turns on approval for the workspace.
evidence.sourceTitle: Manage app approval for your workspace

evidence.claim: To support org-wide installs you add a bot scope, opt in under Org Level Apps (org_deploy_enabled), and an Org Admin approves and installs the app, then chooses workspaces.
assistant:write is a bot scope that lets the app act as an AI assistant app and call assistant.threads.setStatus, setSuggestedPrompts, and setTitle.
channels:history lets the app view messages in public channels it has been added to. It covers conversations.history, conversations.replies, and message events such as message.channels.
Slack rate limit tiers are per method, per workspace, per app: Tier 1 is 1+ a minute and Tier 3 is 50+ a minute.
Composio lists Slack and Slackbot under Composio-managed OAuth available.
Existing connected accounts stay on the auth config they were created with. Only new connections use your custom config.
Reasons to bring your own app include your own name on the consent screen, custom scopes, a dedicated rate limit quota, and faster polling than the 15 minute managed minimum.
The authorization endpoint slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize is live.
evidence.note: GET with an invalid client ID returned HTTP 200 and a small page whose script redirects to the same URL with tracked=1. We did not follow it, so we did not see the error shown for an unknown client.

evidence.claim: Developer portal api.slack.com/apps loads and asks you to sign in to your Slack account to create an app.
evidence.note: HTTP 200, page title Slack API: Applications.

evidence.claim: On February 17, 2026 Slack released an MCP server and the Real-time Search API, which grew out of the Data Access API and lets apps fetch relevant Slack data without storing it.
evidence.sourceTitle: Announcing the Slack MCP server and Real-time Search API
evidence.note: Read from the changelog index page at docs.slack.dev/changelog.

evidence.claim: A community article says the grace period for existing unlisted installs ended March 3, 2026. It links no Slack source and conflicts with Slack's changelog.
evidence.sourceTitle: Slack just throttled your OpenClaw agent

evidence.claim: An agent that reads threads on demand across many customer workspaces needs a Marketplace listing to work well in production.
evidence.note: At 1 call a minute and 15 messages per call, catching up on a busy channel takes many minutes per workspace. Only Marketplace and internal apps get normal limits, and Slack's terms point commercial apps to the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Since March 16, 2026 you can mark individual OAuth scopes as optional, so users can install without granting them.
evidence.note: Read from the changelog index page at docs.slack.dev/changelog.

evidence.claim: An unlisted app can read new messages through Events API message events without calling conversations.history, so the reduced limit mostly hurts backfill and on-demand thread reads.
evidence.note: The rate limit change names only conversations.history and conversations.replies. channels:history also grants message events. Not tested, and Marketplace AI rules still discourage storing message data.
